title: Data Structures & Algorithms in C
summary: Build the classics by hand: growable arrays, queues, linked lists, hash tables, trees, heaps, tries and graphs, plus the sorting and searching that go with them.
description: Every serious program stands on a handful of data structures. Here you build them yourself in C, with malloc, pointers and nothing else: a growable array, a ring-buffer queue, a doubly linked list, two kinds of hash table, a binary search tree with deletion, a heap, a trie and a graph. Along the way you write binary search and three classic sorts, and you finish by combining a hash table and a linked list into an LRU cache, the structure behind real caches in browsers and databases.
outcomes: Implement collections, sorting and graph algorithms in C.
